newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Extreme Romanian politician stripped of immunity.
newsitem.headline: Extreme Romanian politician stripped of immunity.

text.p: Romania's Senate voted on Thursday to strip an extreme nationalist, anti-Semitic politician of his parliamentary immunity amid protests by the opposition which called it unconstitutional and walked out.
Senator Corneliu Vadim Tudor, former court poet of the late Stalinist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu, could face trial over scores of charges of defamation against individuals and state institutions.
The vote followed a request by the Justice Ministry for the Senate to lift Tudor's immunity and to let prosecutors decide if he had a case to answer. A conviction could mean up to five years in jail.
Tudor attacked the decision and said those behind the 74-3 vote were "bandits".
"I'm hunted because I'm a member of the opposition. This is a dictatorship of the majority. One can't talk about politics under these circumstances," Tudor told reporters.

Opposition senators, led by the Party of Social Democracy (PDSR), walked out of the vote in protest. They said the decision was unconstitutional as it had been endorsed by only a simple majority of the 143-strong upper house and not by two-thirds of the senators as required by the constitution.
Senators of the centrist ruling coalition, which ousted the PDSR in elections last November, rejected the objections as groundless.

Last April, two-thirds of senators, including the PDSR, voted to strip Tudor of parliamentary immunity after he made vitriolic attacks against top officials. He accused former president Ion Iliescu whom Tudor of "subordinating the country to the Jews".
